title: Sample 19-4: Coded Number Riddle

illustrates.quote: g. Substitute an underscore for a blank space within a word.

blocks.features: Flush title line (braille shows zero extra indent), not a centred heading.

blocks.text: Solve the following riddle with the help of the pictures under it.
blocks.features: Given braille shows a uniform indent on every line — built blocked:true.

blocks.text: (9 pictures, arranged in a grid: key, cake, bag, fish, hose, nail, clown, tree, tent)
blocks.features: Nine small print pictures, each with a row of blanks (one per letter of the picture's own name) below it; some blanks are numbered, tying that letter to a position in the final riddle-answer number sequence. Not braille-representable in any candidate block type (F-217/219/222).

blocks.text: Why do golfers carry an extra pair of socks?

Picture clues are changed to word clues. An underscore is used to indicate unnumbered blanks. The puzzle code symbols are under the letters. A hyphen separates symbols that form a word. Spaces separate each set of symbols.
key _ 23 10   cake 3 14 _ 18   bag _ 4 11   fish _ 19 5 15   hose 8 21 _ 6   nail 20 _ 1 17   clown _ _ 16 _ 2   tree 7 _ 12 9   tent 13 _ 22 _
blocks.features: Each picture's own word, shown with a blank (underscore) or a number under each letter position — the actual print device is nine separate small pictures with blank/number lines beneath, not text; not buildable (F-217/219/222).

The final decode-by-number answer sequence. Solved (word-length pattern 2,4,4,3,1,4,2,3 exactly matches): "IN CASE THEY GET A HOLE IN ONE!" — not itself printed anywhere; it is what the numbered picture-letter blanks spell out once solved. Not braille-buildable regardless (F-217/219/222).
